strings.en: Copied {copied}, skipped {existing} that exist and {missing} that are missing. CSV: {csv}
strings.de: {copied} kopiert, {existing} vorhandene und {missing} fehlende übersprungen. CSV: {csv}

strings.context: Entry of the command palette that runs the key action settings, which opens the settings as a tab. The plain name of what the action does, as short as a menu entry; the key bound to it is shown beside it.
Label of the third tab in the title bar while the settings are open. One word, noun.
Colored field at the left end of the status bar while the settings tab is open. Upper case, a single short word.
Text in the status bar while the settings tab is open: tells that a changed setting is already in effect and written to the file.
Right end of the status bar while the settings tab is open: how many settings were changed since the tab was opened. Takes the number.
Placeholder of the search field above the feature list on the settings tab. One word, verb.
Note at the bottom of the feature list on the settings tab. Says that the settings live in the file config.toml and that every change is written there. The file name stays as it is.
strings.en: Everything lives in config.toml. Every change here is written to it.
strings.de: Alles steht in config.toml. Jede Änderung hier schreibt dorthin.

strings.context: Shown on the settings tab when the search matches no feature and no setting.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: the look of the program, its color scheme. One word, noun.
Line under the heading of the appearance page on the settings tab.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: the language of the interface. One word, noun.
Line under the heading of the language page on the settings tab.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab for the filing module, next to its theme name Hermes. One word, noun.
Line under the heading of the filing page on the settings tab. Hermes is the name of the filing module.
strings.en: Hermes picks up new documents, reads them and files them by your rules.
strings.de: Hermes holt neue Dokumente ab, liest sie und legt sie nach deinen Regeln ab.

strings.context: Heading of a group of settings on the filing page of the settings tab: the folders Hermes works on.
Heading of a group of settings on the filing page of the settings tab: switching Hermes on and how much computing time it takes.
Heading of a group of settings on the filing page of the settings tab: reading text from scans and images (OCR).
Heading of a group of settings on the filing page of the settings tab: the AI that fills in fields. Two letters, an abbreviation.
Name of a setting on the appearance page: which built-in color scheme the look starts from.
Explanation under the color scheme setting: colors from a VS Code theme or from the theme section of the file are laid over the scheme chosen here.

strings.de: Das eingebaute Aussehen. Farben eines VS-Code-Themes oder aus [theme] kommen darüber.

strings.context: Name of the built-in color scheme Cosmic, the look without any setting. A proper name; keep it.
Name of the built-in color scheme with the earlier dark teal look. A proper name or a plain color word.
Name of the built-in color scheme Classic, the look of the old two-panel file managers.
Name of the built-in color scheme Dracula. A proper name; keep it.
Name of a setting on the appearance page: the VS Code color theme file that the config names. Shown read only.
Explanation under the VS Code theme setting: the file named in the config is laid over the color scheme.
strings.en: The theme file named in config.toml, laid over the color scheme.
strings.de: Die Theme-Datei aus der config.toml, über das Farbschema gelegt.

strings.context: Value of the VS Code theme setting when the config names no theme file.
Button next to the VS Code theme setting that opens the card to download a theme. The ellipsis says a card follows.
Name of the setting on the language page: the language of the interface.
Explanation under the language setting: what is chosen here is written to the file, while the quick switch of the function key row only lasts for the session.
strings.en: Written to config.toml. The quick switch lasts for the session only.
strings.de: Wird in die config.toml geschrieben. Der Schnellwechsel gilt nur für diese Sitzung.

strings.context: Name of the setting on the filing page that switches the filing module Hermes on or off.
Explanation under the setting that switches Hermes on: it works in the background while the program runs.
strings.en: Picks up and files documents while ncrs runs.
strings.de: Holt Dokumente ab und legt sie ab, solange ncrs läuft.

strings.context: Value of a switched on setting on the settings tab, next to its checkbox. One word.
Value of a switched off setting on the settings tab, next to its checkbox. One word.
Name of a folder setting on the filing page: a folder from which Hermes picks up new documents. Followed by its theme name.
Theme name next to the inbox folder setting: the pneumatic tube post, where documents arrive.
Explanation under an inbox folder: Hermes picks up documents there.
strings.en: Hermes picks up new documents here.
strings.de: Hier holt Hermes neue Dokumente ab.

strings.context: Name of a folder setting on the filing page: the one folder where Hermes files new documents.
Explanation under the central filing folder.
Name of a folder setting on the filing page: a folder that Hermes only reads. Followed by its theme name.
Explanation under a records folder: Hermes learns from it but moves nothing.
strings.en: Hermes learns from it but moves nothing.
strings.de: Hermes lernt daraus, verschiebt dort aber nichts.

strings.context: Addition under a folder on the filing page when the folder also takes images.
Shown in the folders group on the filing page when no folder is chosen yet.
Button next to a setting that opens the card where it is changed. The ellipsis says a card follows.
Name of the setting on the filing page: how much computing time Hermes may use.
Explanation under the load setting: how much computing time Hermes may take from the machine.
strings.en: How much computing time Hermes may take.
strings.de: Wie viel Rechenzeit Hermes nehmen darf.

strings.context: Fourth choice of the load setting, shown only when the config names a number of workers. Takes the number.
Name of the setting on the filing page for the files that read text from scans and images.
Explanation under the text recognition models: they are downloaded once, after asking.
strings.en: Needed to read scans and images. Downloaded once, after asking.
strings.de: Nötig, um Scans und Bilder zu lesen. Wird einmal geladen, nach Rückfrage.

Status of the text recognition models or the AI model when the files are not there. Lower case.
Button next to a model setting that opens the card to download the model. The ellipsis says a card follows.
Name of the setting on the filing page that lets an AI fill in fields it could not read by rules.
Explanation under the AI setting: it only fills in fields like sender and date, and the change takes effect when the program starts again.
strings.en: Fills in fields like sender and date. Takes effect at the next start.
strings.de: Füllt Felder wie Absender und Datum. Gilt ab dem nächsten Start.

strings.context: Name of the setting on the filing page that tells where the AI runs. Shown read only.
Explanation under the AI provider: it is set in the file and cannot be changed here.
Value of the AI provider setting when the model runs on this machine.
Value of the AI provider setting when the model runs on a server named in the file.
Name of the setting on the filing page that shows the AI model and whether it is there.
Explanation under the AI model: where the local model lives.
strings.en: Runs on this machine, in the data folder of ncrs.
strings.de: Läuft auf diesem Rechner, im Datenordner von ncrs.

strings.context: Status of the AI model on the settings tab when Hermes is not running, so nothing can be said about the model.
Notice in the status bar after a setting was written to the file but only takes effect when the program starts again.
strings.en: Saved in config.toml. Takes effect at the next start.
strings.de: In der config.toml gespeichert. Gilt ab dem nächsten Start.

strings.context: Title of the copy dialog and label of its primary button. Imperative verb, one word.
Title of the move dialog and label of its primary button. Imperative verb, one word.

Dimmed text after the title of the copy and move dialog: how many top-level entries are selected and how large they are. {count} is two or more, {size} is a size like 4.2 GB or an ellipsis while the folders are still being counted.
Same as transfer.summary for exactly one selected entry. {size} is a size or an ellipsis while it is counted.
Label above the number of files in the copy and move dialog when many entries are selected. Plural noun, one word.
Label above the number of folders in the copy and move dialog when many entries are selected. Plural noun, one word.
Label above the total size in the copy and move dialog when many entries are selected. Noun, one word.
Label above the number of entries the size count could not read in the copy and move dialog. Only shown when there are some. Short adjective phrase.
The first names of a large selection, then how many more there are. {names} is a comma separated list of file names, {count} the number left out.
Button in the copy and move dialog that unfolds the list of all selected names. Short verb phrase.
Button in the copy and move dialog that folds the list of selected names away again. Short verb phrase.
Last line of the unfolded name list when it is cut off: how many names are not shown. {count} is the number left out.
Warning in the copy and move dialog: some selected names already exist in the target folder. {count} is two or more.
strings.en: {count} of these names already exist in the target
strings.de: Im Ziel gibt es schon {count} dieser Namen

strings.context: Same as transfer.conflicts for exactly one name that already exists in the target folder.
strings.en: One of these names already exists in the target
strings.de: Im Ziel gibt es schon einen dieser Namen

strings.context: Label of the target folder field in the copy and move dialog, also its placeholder. One word, a preposition.
Label of the choice in the copy and move dialog for what happens when the target already has a name. Reads as the start of a sentence.
Option of the choice for an existing name: ask for each file that is in the way. One word.
Option of the choice for an existing name: replace the file in the target without asking. One word.
Option of the choice for an existing name: leave the file in the target alone and go on. One word.
Hint in the footer of the copy and move dialog: the Tab key switches between the two. Starts with the key name, keep it.
Error under the target field when the typed folder does not exist.
Error under the target field when the typed path is a file, not a folder.
strings.en: The target is not a folder

strings.context: Error under the target field when the target is the folder the selected entries are already in.
strings.en: Source and target are the same folder
strings.de: Quelle und Ziel sind derselbe Ordner

strings.context: Error under the target field when a selected folder would be copied or moved into itself or one of its subfolders.
strings.en: A folder cannot go into itself
strings.de: Ein Ordner kann nicht in sich selbst

strings.context: Error under the target field when the system would not say whether the target folder can be used, for example for lack of permission.
strings.de: Das Ziel lässt sich nicht lesen

strings.context: Dimmed text after the title of the progress dialog of a copy or move: where it goes. {target} is the folder path.
Button of the progress dialog that closes it while the copy or move goes on. Short, like a mode name.
Hint in the footer of the progress dialog: the Escape key stops the job. Starts with the key name, keep it.
